target: rbr-rounds — "The round count of best-response restart and bidirectional improvement"

findings.defect: The paste-ready LaTeX asserts, of the 9-non-sink instance, that "the best response is unique at each round". This is FALSE at round 0, and with the other best response the instance does NOT separate R_BR from all-switches: R_BR takes 1 round, exactly as all-switches does. The instance is therefore an example of the SAME phenomenon the route attributes only to its second (10-non-sink) instance — that R_BR's count depends on which best response is chosen — and not of a stronger one.
findings.evidence: Independent exact recomputation (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_small2.py). At sigma_0 = {3->1,6->3,7->4}, val_sigma = (1/4,0,0,0,0,1/2,0,0,0) with val_sigma(3) = val_sigma(t_0) = 0, so BOTH tau(4)=3 and tau(4)=t_0 are Min best responses. With tau(4)=3: S_sigma={3,7}, C_max={3} (veto and strict alike), R_BR = 2 rounds. With tau(4)=t_0: C_max={3,7}=S_sigma, R_BR = 1 round. val_sigma cross-checked against the componentwise min over all positional tau.

findings.defect: The result is presented as a self-dual, two-player, BSI phenomenon. It is neither: it is a ONE-PLAYER ALL-SWITCHES phenomenon. In SD(K) the observer v (and v') has IN-DEGREE ZERO — no vertex points at it, it is unreachable from everything — and L(u_j) = 0 for every sigma and tau, so the Min half and the self-duality contribute nothing to the K reversals. Deleting the Min player entirely (replace every u_j in the two mixtures by t_0) gives a ONE-PLAYER stopping SSG with Vmin = empty on which plain ALL-SWITCHES switches v exactly K times in K rounds. The self-duality apparatus (two K^2-vertex mixture trees, the Min cascade, the involution) serves only to make the BSI veto vacuous, i.e. it is rbr:lem-vacuous applied — so rbr:prop-sd = (a one-player all-switches construction) + (rbr:lem-vacuous), and should be stated that way. The correct headline is the stronger and simpler one the route does not make: prop:allswitch-overshoot's record of three switches at one vertex under all-switches extends to Theta(N) by construction, with one player.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_sd2.py: in-edges into v = [] and into v' = [] for K=3,4,5,6; all-switches alone on SD(K) has switch multiset {v: K, x_j: 1 each}. t_one.py builds the stripped one-player game SD1(K): K=3,4,5,6,8 give N=28,37,51,60,87, |Vmin|=0, stopping, all-switches rounds = K, v switched K times. Also note K rounds against |C| = 2K+2, so SD(K) is nowhere near any round ceiling.

findings.defect: Prior-art risk not flagged. FROM MEMORY, UNCHECKED AGAINST THE SOURCE: van Dijk, Loho and Maat have a paper on the worst-case complexity of symmetric strategy improvement, which I believe establishes an EXPONENTIAL lower bound for that rule on parity games. If that recollection is right, the route's central open question — the round count of def:bsi — is already answered negatively in the literature for the parity-game form of the same rule, and the whole route is chasing a family that exists in print. rbr:rem-attr says only "we do not know of a published family separating either rule from all-switches", which is a strictly narrower claim than "no published lower bound" and does not discharge this. The route (and rem:bsi-br, which already attributes def:bsi to those authors) must record the risk explicitly.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:bsi-br already attributes def:bsi to van Dijk--Loho--Maat and R_BR to its one-track variant, and says "if it holds then the round count of def:bsi is their open question and not ours" — so the document already knows the rule is theirs, and the lower-bound literature for it was not checked. No web access was used; this is a memory flag, not a citation.

findings.defect: Proved only for the STRICT variant, while the headline and the results summary say "forces BOTH BSI tracks to be long" without qualification — and def:bsi proper is the VETO variant, which is the one on which the document's only long-ish runs occur (rbr:prop-q16 shows three of Q_16's four reversals are ties that the strict variant refuses). But the restriction is UNNECESSARY: the theorem holds for the veto variant too, by the paper's own lem:bsi-pairloc. Proof: at a productive veto-variant round with C_min = empty, M > 0 (else thm:bsi-nostall gives a halt) and the strict-variant C_min^< is contained in C_min = empty, so lem:bsi-pairloc (stated there for both variants) gives Z intersect C_max^> nonempty, hence |C_max^>| >= 1 and Phi(sigma',U) >= Phi(sigma,U)+1. So within a maximal block of consecutive C_min = empty rounds Phi strictly increases, blocks have length <= m, blocks number <= B+1, and A <= m(1+B), R <= m+(m+1)B for def:bsi as written. The same block argument also makes the D-bookkeeping of rbr:lem-greedy redundant: the whole theorem is "with U frozen the Max track runs at most m rounds", i.e. prop:bsi-oneplayer relativised, in three lines.
findings.evidence: Proof above from lem:bsi-pairloc (frontier.tex line 6391) and thm:bsi-nostall (line 6355). Empirically consistent: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_block.py, 206 veto-variant rounds with C_min empty drawn from random stopping games, 0 with C_max^> empty; t_track.py, 1022 runs of both variants, 0 violations of sum|C_max| <= m+mB, R <= m+(m+1)B, R <= k+(k+1)A.

findings.result_name: rbr:thm-track, corollary "BSI is polynomial whenever min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|) = O(log N)"
findings.defect: Stated without the remark that makes it honest: the class min(m,k) = O(log N) is TRIVIALLY in P, by enumerating the smaller player's 2^{min(m,k)} = poly(N) positional strategies and taking the componentwise extremum of the resulting one-player values (w* = min over positional tau of val^tau, each val^tau computable by thm:one-player's LP). So the corollary is a statement about the RULE, not a new polynomial class, and it is a one-line generalisation of thm:one-player (the min = 0 case). As written a reader will take it for a seventh polynomial class.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex thm:one-player (line 2032) gives val for Vmin = empty by one LP; determinacy plus positional optimality of Min gives w* = min_tau val^tau. The route's own text does not say the class is trivially decidable.

findings.defect: "It also raises the largest BSI round count known here from 11 (round 14's annealing) to Theta(N)" is false as a statement about what is achievable: Theta(N) BSI rounds is obtained by an eight-line ONE-PLAYER cascade, and by prop:bsi-oneplayer's own bound |Vmax| being attained. The "11" was a search artefact, not a record.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_cascade.py: the cascade x_j -> (x_{j-1}, k_j) with val(k_j) = 1 - 2^{-j}, N = 2K+2, Vmin empty, gives all-switches = BSI = K rounds for K = 3,5,8,12. (Incidentally the ladder L_n gives BSI = 1 round for n = 3,4,6,8, which is a datum the document does not have.)

findings.defect: "Refuting the standing belief that best-response restart is never slower" attacks a belief that frontier.tex does not hold. rem:bsi-br records exactly two measurements (L_n, G#) and states in terms that "the round count of R_BR is open, exactly as that of def:bsi is". The theorem itself is correct and new in this document; the framing is not. Separately, the significance should be calibrated: RD(n) has all-switches BA height 1 from EVERY Max strategy, R_BR = n = |Vmax| and BSI = 2n = |C|, all at the natural ceiling for a rule that switches one vertex per round (thm:short-path), so the family is no progress on the pivot and no progress on any lower bound — its content is purely the removal of the two data points that favoured R_BR.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:bsi-br, lines 6609-6665. Independent verification of RD(n) in exact arithmetic (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-rbr/t_rd.py): n = 2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12 give N = 9n, stopping, all-switches = 1, R_BR = n (both variants), BSI = 2n (both variants); exhaustive over all 2^n Max starts for n <= 4 gives all-switches worst case 1 and R_BR worst case n; val_sigma cross-checked against the componentwise min over all positional tau.

findings.defect: Two problems. (a) DEPENDENCY: the lemma is derived from bsr:prop-selfdual, which is NOT in frontier.tex — the string "self-dual" occurs zero times in the document; it is round 14's unintegrated bsi-rounds route. Nothing here can be integrated until that proposition is. (b) STRENGTH: given bsr:prop-selfdual the lemma is a one-line substitution (mirror-pairing turns that proposition's veto L(phi sigma-bar(v)) <= L(phi sigma(v)) into L(sigma(v)) <= L(sigma-bar(v)), automatic on S_sigma), and its transfer is only a SUFFICIENCY: it is useful only if the mirror-paired class realises AUSOs of superpolynomial BA height, and the route's own search found exactly m rounds at m = 1,2,3,4 against h*(m) = 1,2,4,7. The route does not state the sharp missing question, which is: can a mirror-paired self-dual stopping SSG have an all-switches run longer than |Vmax| rounds? If not, rbr:lem-vacuous is vacuous.

findings.defect: Two claims rest on random sampling and by the standing rule are unsupported as evidence: "a random search over stopping games with up to 14 non-sinks ... produced no run exceeding |C| rounds" and "hours of random restart plus hill climbing ... produced longest all-switches runs 1,2,3,4". verdict:
IS IT NEW? Mostly yes, with two exceptions and one big caveat. rbr:thm-readout (RD(n)) is the one clearly new object in the route: a proved family on which R_BR takes n rounds and BSI 2n where all-switches takes 1 from every Max strategy. Nothing in frontier.tex does this; thm:ladder separates least-index from all-switches (exponentially), thm:all-switches-refuted separates a single switch from all-switches on 5 vertices, and neither touches a val^tau-guided rule. rbr:lem-greedy/rbr:thm-track is new as a statement but is prop:bsi-oneplayer relativised — its real content is one sentence ("with U frozen the Max track runs at most m rounds"), and the D-bookkeeping is redundant. rbr:prop-sd is NOT new in the way it is sold (see finding 2): stripped of decoration it is a one-player all-switches construction that extends prop:allswitch-overshoot's three-switches-at-one-vertex to Theta(N), and the self-duality only transports it to BSI via rbr:lem-vacuous. rbr:lem-constant is cor:comparison. rbr:lem-vacuous is a one-line corollary of an unintegrated round-14 proposition. rbr:prop-slowlevel largely re-illustrates cor:bsi-levels' own printed caveat. The route's attributions of def:bsi/R_BR are correct and inherited from rem:bsi-br; the "readout" device is correctly credited to the solo round. The unflagged prior-art risk is the lower-bound literature for symmetric strategy improvement (finding 3).

IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No claimed algorithm and no target-equivalent oracle. No barrier is claimed. The only class-shaped claim is "BSI is polynomial when min(m,k) = O(log N)", and that class is trivially decidable by enumerating the smaller player's strategies (finding 5) — the statement is about the rule only and must say so. rbr:lem-vacuous is a conditional transfer whose usefulness is unknown and may be nil. RD(n) and SD(K) are genuine families: build(n), stopping (verified by lem:trapchar), out-degree two, fair coins, measured at >= 4 sizes with proofs.

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Yes, with one false statement. Everything I re-derived independently in exact arithmetic checked out except rbr:prop-small's uniqueness claim, which is false and weakens what that instance shows (finding 1). The two random-sampling claims are correctly labelled as open/measured.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. The route's GAP is a proposed counter ARCHITECTURE, not the missing object. The missing object is: a stopping SSG family on N = n^{O(1)} vertices and a pair start on which def:bsi performs superpolynomially many productive rounds. By rbr:thm-track — extended to def:bsi proper as in finding 4 — such a family must have BOTH A and B superpolynomial, hence min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|) = omega(log N), so it cannot be one-player and cannot be a disjoint union. The route's own rbr:lem-vacuous supplies the only reduction it has, and that reduction is unusable until a cheaper question is settled, which the route should have marked as its GAP and did not: CAN A MIRROR-PAIRED SELF-DUAL STOPPING SSG HAVE AN ALL-SWITCHES RUN LONGER THAN |Vmax| ROUNDS? If no, rbr:lem-vacuous is vacuous and the route's next_steps (3) is dead; if yes, the route's problem is a strict specialisation of the all-switches pivot (cor:ceiling-general), not an independent problem. Neither RD(n) nor SD(K) moves any lower bound: both are linear, both sit at or below |C| rounds, RD(n) has all-switches BA height 1, and SD(K) has K rounds against |C| = 2K+2.

INTEGRATE? NET BETTER, but only after edits; roughly half the route should not go in. WORTH INTEGRATING: (i) rbr:thm-readout and rbr:def-rd, verbatim modulo the "standing belief"/"raises the record" rhetoric, which is wrong (findings 6, 7) — this is the route's real contribution and it settles a question rem:bsi-br leaves open; (ii) rbr:lem-greedy/rbr:thm-track, rewritten in three lines as the block argument, EXTENDED to the veto variant via lem:bsi-pairloc (finding 4), and with the triviality caveat on the min(m,k) corollary (finding 5) — the quantitative "both tracks must be long" sharpens rem:bsi-gap's qualitative "must be genuinely two-player"; (iii) rbr:prop-q16, two sentences: Q_16's four reversals are three L-ties plus one strict switch, so round 14's four-switch record is a veto-variant tie artefact and the strict record there was one; (iv) rbr:lem-constant as a footnote to cor:comparison. WORTH INTEGRATING ONLY AFTER REWRITING: rbr:prop-sd, restated as a ONE-PLAYER proposition — "there is a one-player stopping SSG on O(K^2) vertices with |Vmax| = K+1 on which all-switches switches one vertex K times", superseding prop:allswitch-overshoot's three — followed by one line saying rbr:lem-vacuous carries it to BSI; the current two-player self-dual presentation hides that the observer is unreachable and that no Min player is needed. NOT WORTH INTEGRATING: rbr:prop-gain (finding 9); the rbr:rem-psd witness matrices (three 4x4 matrices of measured, non-transferable content that prop:auso-size says can prove nothing); rbr:prop-small as written (fix the false parenthetical or drop the first instance, keeping only the 10-non-sink one, which makes the same point correctly); rbr:prop-slowlevel beyond one sentence. And rbr:def-psd/rbr:lem-vacuous cannot be integrated at all until round 14's bsr:prop-selfdual is, since "self-dual" does not occur in frontier.tex.
